claims.text: French archive history; Dillon US recommendation Different institutions

The French diplomatic archive distinguishes colonial AOF, later seated at Dakar, from the Mali Federation. Dillon’s 1960 memorandum recommends separate U.S. recognition for Senegal and Mali. Shared earlier administration did not make these institutions identical; recognition is a particular diplomatic act, not universal consent.
Were AOF and the Mali Federation the same institution continuing unchanged? Different institutions; Senegal and Mali became separate actors

claims.text: Does a shared Senegal/Sudan membership prove AOF continued as the Mali Federation? No. The acquired archive distinguishes the institutions; the 1960 memorandum treats Senegal and Mali separately.
French custodians/editors are not the African historical actors. AOF and the Mali Federation remain distinct; Dillon’s U.S. recommendation is not universal recognition or popular assent.
